prompt: You put $100 in a savings account that pays 5% interest a year, and you leave the interest in the account. After two years, how much will you have?
explanation: In the first year you earn 5% of $100, which is $5, so your balance becomes $105. In the second year you earn 5% of $105, which is $5.25, giving $110.25. That extra 25 cents is compound interest: interest earned on interest already added. Over many years, that snowball is what makes saving early so powerful.
